title: Reverse Part of a List

concept.title: Reverse in place by pulling nodes to the front of the block
body: Reverse only the nodes from position `left` to position `right` (counting from 1), and leave the rest. First walk to the node `prev` that stands **just before** the block (use a dummy node, so that `left = 1` also works). The first node of the block, `cur`, will end up as the **last** node of the reversed block.
Then repeat `right - left` times: take the node **after** `cur` and move it to the front of the block (right after `prev`). This reverses the block step by step, in place.

body.code:
for _ in range(right - left):
    nxt = cur.next
    cur.next = nxt.next        # cut nxt out
    nxt.next = prev.next       # put nxt in front of the block
    prev.next = nxt

body: `cur` never moves: it keeps its place while more nodes are pulled in front of it, so after the loop it is at the end of the reversed block and already points to the first node after the block.

statement: Reverse the nodes of a singly linked list from position `left` to position `right` (both included, counting from 1) and print the whole list.
inputFormat: The second line has the values of the nodes, from the head to the tail.
outputFormat: Print the values of the new list on one line.
hints: Use a dummy node and walk `left - 1` steps to the node before the block.
The first node of the block stays in place while the following nodes are moved to the front of the block.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

# Every node is also remembered in this list. Python in the browser cannot free a very long chain of nodes at once,
# so free_nodes() (called at the end) cuts the links first and the nodes are then freed one by one.
all_nodes = []


class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next
        all_nodes.append(self)


def free_nodes():
    for node in all_nodes:
        node.next = None
        if hasattr(node, "random"):
            node.random = None
    all_nodes.clear()


# Builds a list from the values. If pos is 0 or more, the last node points back to the node at index pos (a cycle).
def build_list(values, pos=-1):
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = ListNode(v, head)
    if pos >= 0:
        tail = head
        while tail.next is not None:
            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        for _ in range(pos):
            target = target.next
        tail.next = target
    return head


# Prints the values of a list on one line ("empty" for an empty list).
def print_list(head):
    out = []
    while head is not None:
        out.append(head.val)
        head = head.next
    print(*(out if out else ["empty"]))


def reverse_between(head, left, right):
    dummy = ListNode(0, head)
    prev = dummy
    for _ in range(left - 1):
        prev = prev.next
    cur = prev.next
    for _ in range(right - left):
        nxt = cur.next
        cur.next = nxt.next
        nxt.next = prev.next
        prev.next = nxt
    return dummy.next

n, left, right = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

print_list(reverse_between(build_list(a), left, right))
free_nodes()
